examples.question_text: A vehicle has a stopping distance of $85$ m and a reaction distance of $24$ m. Calculate its braking distance.
A vehicle has a stopping distance of $57$ m and a braking distance of $33$ m. Calculate its reaction distance.

A car travels at $78$ km/h and the driver takes $1.6$ s to react. Its braking distance is estimated by $d=0.01v^2$, where $d$ is in metres and $v$ is in km/h. Calculate the total stopping distance to one decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Reaction distance uses speed in m/s, so divide the speed in km/h by $3.6$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Reaction distance} &= \frac{78}{3.6}\times1.6\\&=\frac{104}{3}\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

The braking formula requires speed in km/h, so use $v=78$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Braking distance} &=0.01\times78^2\\&=60.84\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

Add the distances, retaining the unrounded reaction distance until the final step.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Stopping distance} &=\frac{104}{3}+60.84\\&\approx95.5\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
